the measurement of the matter energy and Hubble parameter directly using the large scale structure is possible.
the growth rate measurement at z ≥ 3.5 will enable the direct measurements of Ωm0 and H0 with the less than 3% and 5% error levels, respectively.

we have developed a method to measure the present value of matter energy density contrast (Ωm0) and the Hubble constant (H0) from the growth rate of the large scale structure, which is independent of the value of Hubble constant.

the method to measure the Hubble parameter and the matter energy density directly from the measurement the linear growth rate of the Universe.
the method to measure directly the present value of matter energy density and the evolution of the Universe from the measurement of large scale structure.

the method of measuring both the present value and the Hubble evolution of the matter energy densities directly from large scale structure of Universe, without any prior information on the current value of H0.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, the measurement of the growth of the linear density perturbations is an important and useful method in order to measure the cosmological parameters, especially the matter energy density Ωm0 and the Hubble parameters H(z).

the measurement of the growth factor and Hubble parameter is an efficient and robust method for measuring the matter energy density Ωm0 and the evolution of the expansion rate H(z) without the assumption of the cosmological model.
the method to obtain the present value of Ωm0 and H0 from the measurement of linear growth rate is a promising way for the future large scale structure galaxy survey.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can measure the matter energy density Ωm0 and the Hubble rate H(z) directly from the measurement the linear growth rate of large scale structure of galaxies.
the measurement of the matter density contrast is more robust than the estimation of the Hubble parameters.
the growth rate measurement is a promising method to constrain cosmological parameters, especially the Hubble parameter, if the measurement of the growth rates can be reached at the high redshift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth rate measurement is a powerful probe to measure the present value of Ωm0, and the evolution of Hubble parameter.
the measurement of the matter density contrast Ωm0 and the evolution of Hubble parameter H(z) can be obtained from the measurement of growth rate of the large scale structure.
